messages:
Jordan: quick handoff — taking primary off-shift, handing to Priya. overnight summary: at ~00:45 UTC we saw a sudden surge of 429s and client-side timeouts hitting request-router in us-west. incident-bot paged with 'route-backpressure' at 00:47. Impact: elevated 429s for ~1.2% of short-lived API requests and some healthcheck churn; a few Dedicated customers reported intermittent 504s via CSMs. no persistent data loss. actions, timeline, and follow-ups below.

incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered: route-backpressure (severity P2) at 00:47 UTC. Affected services: request-router-usw, request-proxy. Suggested runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/route-backpressure

Jordan: timeline + actions I executed (timestamps UTC):
- 00:49: scaled up request-router-usw replicas 4 -> 7 as an emergency capacity bump via k8s (kubectl scale deploy/request-router-usw --replicas=7).
- 00:52: temporarily enabled per-customer soft-queueing to avoid thundering-herds (config flag: routing.soft_queue=true) for 10m window.
- 00:55: applied filter to reject overly-aggressive healthcheck cram from internal infra (ip-range block on lb config).
- 01:02: added a short 10s token bucket backpressure for unauthenticated ingress to reduce noise.
- 01:10: engaged CS to notify the two affected Dedicated customers; ops-bot verified no deploys during incident window.
- left brief notes in incident doc + captured request traces for top offenders.

Priya: taking primary. I read the runbook and Jordan's notes. immediate checks on my list:
- confirm autoscaler didn't bounce pods and that new replicas are healthy
- verify that soft-queueing is honoring per-customer limits and not dropping legitimate traffic
- check ingress LB metrics and rate-limit counters
- confirm there are no backlog spikes in downstream services (frontend-proxy, rate-limiter)

ops-bot: Deploy bot: no user deploys to request-router-usw between 23:30-01:30 UTC. Autoscaler events: scaled from 3->7 at 00:49 per manual scale.

Lee: I can assist on monitoring and logs. flagged a suspicious client id that sent many small parallel requests right at 00:44 — likely automated retry loop. added to incident doc.

Priya: immediate checks done:
- replicas 7 healthy, readiness probes pass
- soft-queueing showing queued_count ~120 (within expected), drop_rate ~0.2%
- ingress LB shows sustained spike in SYNs from a small set of source IPs, correlated with the client id Lee flagged
- downstream latency (frontend-proxy p95) returned to baseline after scale-up

Priya: mitigation plan I'll own until 10:00 UTC:
1) keep soft-queueing enabled for 30m and monitor queue drain
2) keep scaled replicas at 7 for 45m then allow autoscaler to manage if stable
3) request CS to get the Dedicated customers to confirm no active retries from their side; escalate if they do not respond in 20m
4) if 429s climb above 1% again, enable a stricter server-side concurrency limit per-customer and roll back soft-queueing to reject policy
links: https://dashboards.redwood/router-429s, https://redwood.internal/runbooks/route-backpressure

Jordan: FYI — root cause hypothesis: a misconfigured client retry loop (exponential backoff disabled) plus a small rolling deploy on the customer's side that coincided with our traffic peak. suggested longer-term fixes: per-customer concurrency caps, better client-side guidance in docs, and a circuit-breaker in the proxy. opened OPS-3220 for the circuit-breaker RFC.

Priya: status update 01:35 UTC: 429 rate dropped to 0.18% from peak 1.2%, queue drained to ~30, no new 504 reports for Dedicated customers in last 20m. keeping soft-queueing active and monitoring.

Lee: added a log snippet to incident doc showing the offending client id headers and request patterns. CS reached out and confirmed one of the customers had an internal job misconfigured. they've paused it.

Priya: customer comms: Jordan opened CS ticket CS-1981 and posted a short status to the affected account teams. Recommend a follow-up note to customers tomorrow with root cause and the mitigation we applied.

Priya: handoff summary for next shift (please pass to whoever's next):
- current status: stable with mitigations active (soft-queueing enabled, replicas temporarily bumped to 7). 429s trending down to baseline. Dedicated customers notified and one job paused.
- open items for next oncall:
  * monitor router 429 p95/p99 and queue depth for 60m
  * if steady for 45m, remove manual replica bump and let HPA manage
  * follow-up on OPS-3220 (circuit-breaker RFC) and escalate if more customers affected
  * ensure CS posts customer-facing RCA after full investigation
- coverage gaps: we had limited SRE coverage from 01:00-02:00 UTC (single engineer on rotation), consider adding extra rotation during planned bulk-job windows for better response time.
- runbook pointers: runbook://route-backpressure, runbook://per-customer-concurrency, ops://OPS-3220

oncall-rotation-bot: Reminder: Priya is primary until 10:00 UTC, Lee is secondary for this shift.

Jordan: thanks all — logging out. Priya, leaving the incident doc in 'monitoring' state, please escalate to P1 if customer impact increases.

Priya: will do. I'll update INC-7310 with final notes and assign postmortem skeleton to Lee.

participants: Jordan, Priya, Lee, incident-bot, ops-bot, oncall-rotation-bot
